text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED: DNS resolution errors observed for inference.redwood.ai in eu-west region. Severity: P2. Potential customer impact: failed model calls, increased latency. Paging oncall: @alex_k and @jordan_sre.

alex_k: seeing a spike of SERVFAILs and NXDOMAIN from several customers, started ~09:12 UTC. Alerts: high 5xx from frontend (dns resolution failures). Affected region: eu-west-1.

jordan_sre: confirmed from our probes — intermittent NXDOMAIN from Cloudflare public resolvers to our geo-records. Starting triage.

alex_k: sample dig from our probe:```bash
dig +short @1.1.1.1 inference.redwood.ai ANY
;; -> response: ;; status: SERVFAIL
;; ANSWER: (none)
```

alex_k: curl from app node to model endpoint yields:```bash
curl -sv https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/health -H 'Host: inference.redwood.ai'
* TCP connection established
* Server returned HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

rita_netops: Cloudflare Status shows increased 1xx/5xx for their resolver cluster in eu. Also seeing EDNS truncation anomalies in packet captures. Could be upstream peering or rate-limiting. Opening ticket with CF.

lena_cs: Customer reports: "we saw a cascade of errors for ~10 minutes then some requests recovered" — they're on eu cluster. Marking for SLO impact.

jordan_sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase Route53 health check weight to shift traffic off affected geo records; 2) adjust TTLs to lower so changes propagate faster; 3) add explicit resolver fallback to 8.8.8.8/9.9.9.9 from our egress proxies. Thoughts?

alex_k: prefer Route53 change + lower TTL. Quick confirmation: our geoDNS policy has primary CF, secondary AWS Route53 weighted record. If CF resolvers returning SERVFAIL while Route53 healthy, we need to force clients to route via route53 answers. But many clients use CF/1.1.1.1 which queries CF authoritative chain, not our choice. So we must 1) ensure Route53 answers are more attractive via lower TTL + update weights and 2) if possible, push Cloudflare to clear caches.

rita_netops: suggested runbook commands:```bash
# lower TTL on zone (example)
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.redwood.ai.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-route","TTL":30,"Weight":100,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.3.3.3"}]}}]}'
# add health check or increase weight to Route53 target
```

alex_k: applying TTL=30 and shifting weight to Route53 now. I'll run change and post refs.

deploy-bot: Change-request started: CR-2893 by alex_k — route53 UPSERT queued.

alex_k: change applied. Route53 now TTL=30 and weight EU=100. Waiting for propagation.

jordan_sre: added temporary egress resolver fallback on proxy fleet (rolling):```bash
for node in $(list-proxy-nodes --region eu-west-1); do
  ssh $node 'sudo sed -i "s/^nameserver .*/nameserver 9.9.9.9/" /etc/resolv.conf && systemctl restart network'
done
```

rita_netops: CF responded — they're seeing a subset of their resolver POPs returning SERVFAIL due to EDNS buffer/MTU path issues. They are doing an active flush and peering checks. They recommend keeping TTL low for ~10 minutes and then revert.

alex_k: monitoring metrics — DNS error rate decreasing from 6% -> 1.2% across eu in ~6 minutes. Some clients still failing.

lena_cs: updating customer with status: "we mitigated routing and continue monitoring; some residual errors may persist — will update when fully resolved".

jordan_sre: next steps: keep TTL=30 for 15 minutes, keep Route53 weight high, monitor resolver errors. If error rate does not drop below 0.5% -> escalate to P1 and prepare cross-region failover of inference traffic to eu-central.

rita_netops: note for postmortem: capture CF support ticket id, traceroutes showing EDNS fragmentation, and packet captures. Also track whether our CDN or WAF influenced EDNS size or flags.

mike_platform: preparing a canary config to shift a small % to eu-central for risk-free validation if needed.

alex_k: 09:31 UTC — majority traffic recovered; still watching. Marking incident as "mitigation in progress".

deploy-bot: automation note: rolling resolver fallback applied to 40 proxy nodes.

alex_k: handing off to night oncall @mike_platform for follow-up and post-incident actions. Summary for handoff: root cause suspected Cloudflare resolver POP EDNS/MTU path issue causing SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN to our GeoDNS chain; mitigation: lowered TTL on Route53, shifted weight to Route53 answers, added resolver fallback on egress proxies. Continue monitoring metrics and revert TTL after 20m if stable.

mike_platform: ack — I'll own the remainder. Will coordinate postmortem doc and make sure CS tickets have timeline.

lena_cs: thanks team — I'll keep customer updated and capture timelines for their SLA hit.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity downgraded to P3. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.

alex_k: leaving channel. Good job team. :thumbsup:

mike_platform: logging runbook actions to /incidents/2912345678/postmortem-draft.md and will include CF ticket and packet captures.

rita_netops: follow-up reminder: check peering MTU and EDNS settings on our authoritative nameservers; schedule a resilience test for alternate resolver paths.

mike_platform: last check 09:55 UTC — DNS error rate <0.2% in eu. I'll close if stable for another 10m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (provisional): 10:05 UTC — monitoring period passed, service normalized. Close after postmortem completed. :white_check_mark:
